commit.message:
docs: describe the agent_step telemetry span (#24309)

## Background

The GenAI telemetry reference for `generateText` / `streamText` lists
three span types and says the `chat` span sits under the root span.
Since #14614 the `OpenTelemetry` integration also creates a `step {n}`
span (`INTERNAL`, `gen_ai.operation.name: "agent_step"`) per step, and
`chat` and `execute_tool` spans are nested under it. The docs never
mention that span, so it is hard to tell orchestration steps apart from
model calls.

## Summary

Added the `step {n}` span to the list, noted that `agent_step` is an AI
SDK-specific operation name, and fixed the `chat` span parent. I also
updated the deprecated object API section, since `generateObject` /
`streamObject` don't create a step span and their `chat` span is a
direct child of the root.

commit.message:
fix(open-responses): emit response-metadata on response.created event in doStream (#23959)

## Background

In `@ai-sdk/open-responses` (and downstream `@ai-sdk/quiverai`),
`generateText` preserves the server's `response.id`, `response.modelId`,
and `response.timestamp`, but `streamText` drops them because the stream
transform in `doStream` was missing a handler for the server-sent
`response.created` event.

As a result, streaming fell back to core defaults (a synthetic
`aitxt-...` ID, local client clock, and the requested model ID instead
of the served one). This broke downstream telemetry, audit trails, and
multi-turn response chaining (`previous_response_id`), creating an
inconsistency with `generateText` and sibling providers like
`@ai-sdk/openai`.

## Summary

- Handled `chunk.type === 'response.created'` in
`packages/open-responses/src/responses/open-responses-language-model.ts`,
enqueuing a `response-metadata` part with the server-provided `id`,
`timestamp` (safe null-guarded Unix second conversion), and `modelId`
(matching the pattern in
`packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts`).
- Added unit test coverage in
`packages/open-responses/src/responses/open-responses-language-model.test.ts`
verifying that `response.created` emits `response-metadata`.
- Updated test snapshots where recorded chunk fixtures
(`lmstudio-basic.1`, `lmstudio-tool-call.1`, `openai-pdf-input-file.1`)
included `response.created`.
- Added patch changeset for `@ai-sdk/open-responses`.

## Contributor Credit

- Issue reporter: @shpetimhaxhiu for reporting #23869 and providing the
initial audit.
- @suryakant-source for the failing test reproduction in #23877.

## End-to-End Verification

Tested with an SSE stream containing `response.created` followed by text
deltas. Verified that `streamText` emits the `response-metadata` part
immediately upon `response.created`, matching `generateText` output for
the same server payload. All 134 test cases in `@ai-sdk/open-responses`
pass on both Node and Edge environments.

merged)

commit.message:
feat(workflow): remove experimental_transform from WorkflowAgent.stream() (#24417)

## Background

`experimental_transform` on `WorkflowAgent.stream()` did not work
reliably with workflow steps:

- `@ai-sdk/workflow` had its own `StreamTextTransform` type that
operated on raw provider stream parts (`LanguageModelV4StreamPart`).
Core's `StreamTextTransform` operates on processed `TextStreamPart`
values, so the two share a name but not the same types. Transforms
written for `streamText`, such as `smoothStream`, do not work with
`WorkflowAgent`.
- Core applies one transform instance across the whole multi-step
stream. In `WorkflowAgent`, each model call runs in its own `'use
step'`, so the transform was rebuilt in every step. Any state a
transform kept was lost between steps and on replay.
- `stopStream()` only cancelled the current step's provider stream, not
the agent loop as it does in core.
- The option was only wired into `stream()`. `generate()` never accepted
it.

## Summary

- Removed `experimental_transform` from `WorkflowAgent.stream()`
options, from `ModelCallOptions`, and from the model-call iterator
plumbing.
- Removed the `StreamTextTransform` type and its export from
`@ai-sdk/workflow`.
- Removed the transform wrapping in `do-stream-step.ts` and the
`applyStreamTransforms` helper.

Core `streamText` and `experimental_transform` are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)

commit.message:
feat(tools-registry): add cleave (#24353)

## Background

Add Cleave's published AI SDK tool package to the Tools Registry. The
tools plan swaps as unsigned calls, track plans, find tokens and submit
gas orders that an external wallet has already signed.

## Summary

Add one `cleave` entry for `@cleave-protocol/ai-sdk`, with install
commands, a direct AI SDK guide and a planning-only example. Clarify
that signed gas-order submission uses `needsApproval` by default. No
private keys or signing capability are provided by the package.

Independent checks: the exact snippet compiles against
`@cleave-protocol/ai-sdk@0.1.1` and local SDK declarations. Static
inspection confirms the four tool factories, default conditional
approval for an input containing a signature, documented per-chain
address checks and refusal output. The integration guide and published
source agree with the example. Package metadata includes npm provenance.
Full workspace type checking, lint and repository verifiers pass. Claude
Code CLI with `--model opus` reviewed exact final commit
`e1fcd4c59b4ae94c307ff98dee8fb8e4b4cbaff3` and found no blockers. Its
earlier suggestion to lowercase the sample wallet address is
incorporated. The existing SpecStream, M91 and Olostep entries are
preserved unchanged after resolving the final registry conflict against
current main. The example retains the lowercase address to avoid
checksum ambiguity. No SDK runtime code or repository dependencies
change.

## Contributor Credit

@cleave-protocol contributed the entry and live-service verification.
The signed replacement commit preserves contributor authorship.

## End-to-End Verification

Independent verification is limited to package source/declaration
inspection, the exact example's type check and reading the linked
integration guide. The newest package tarball was downloaded without
lifecycle scripts strictly for static inspection; its JavaScript was not
executed. No wallet was connected, no signing occurred and no
transaction or signed gas order was submitted. No model-provider
credentials are configured. These checks do not constitute a live E2E
run.

Contributor evidence retained from the original PR: `generateText` with
a scripted model called the live Cleave API for a 25 USDC to WETH plan
on Base and received a request ID plus two unsigned calls; runs were
reported with AI SDK 7/Zod 4 and AI SDK 6/Zod 3.25, ESM and CJS. The
contributor also reported type-checking the example against 0.1.0. Those
results were not independently rerun; independent declaration review
used 0.1.1.

The registry contains this complete example (a live run requires
model/Gateway credentials):

```ts
import { generateText, isStepCount } from 'ai';
import { cleaveTools } from '@cleave-protocol/ai-sdk';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5-mini',
  prompt:
    'Plan a swap of 25 USDC to WETH on Base for wallet 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000a11ce.',
  tools: cleaveTools(),
  stopWhen: isStepCount(5),
});

console.log(text);
```

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [ ] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Future Work

The package's README documents that its checks do not validate price,
route, output amount, nested bridge/composer recipients, amounts for
tokens with unknown decimals, or an upper bound on the quoted Stargate
messaging fee. This registry review is not a wallet-security audit. The
package recommends human review before wallet signing.

including it for the request

## Background

Registry. The entry shows how `toolApproval` gates a selected tool
before execution.

## Summary

Add `@msg91comm/m91` with direct integration documentation and a
complete `createM91ToolApproval` example. The sample refund executor
explicitly returns a simulated result and tells applications to replace
it with their payment API before issuing real refunds.

The exact example compiles against `@msg91comm/m91@1.2.0` and the local
SDK. The published package exports the documented integration. Full
workspace types and lint pass. Claude Code CLI with `--model opus`
reviewed exact final commit `46c78212a3b4b7a6c86c15d4a3a42edafc942c67`
and found no blockers. The existing SpecStream entry and the previously
verified M91 example are preserved unchanged on current main. No runtime
SDK code or dependencies change.

## Contributor Credit

@anshiikkach contributed the registry entry and tool-approval example.
The signed replacement commit preserves contributor authorship.

## End-to-End Verification

Independently ran a local public `generateText` tool loop with the
actual published `createM91ToolApproval` implementation and local
workspace SDK. Approval asks once and executes the simulation once;
rejection and a service exception each ask once and execute zero times.
All three runs complete. Global fetch is disabled, and no phone
notification, voice call, real refund or external client action is sent.

This is a synthetic application replay with injected model and approval
client, not a live M91 or model-provider E2E run. No M91 or inference
credentials are configured; phone delivery and live service behavior
remain unverified. Package source and integration docs corroborate the
displayed API.

Prerequisites: supported Node/pnpm and installed workspace dependencies.
Save the complete script below outside the checkout as
`/tmp/ai-m91/verify.mjs`. Build the checkout's packages and prepare a
temporary dependency directory:

```bash
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai...
mkdir -p /tmp/ai-m91
npm install --prefix /tmp/ai-m91 --ignore-scripts @msg91comm/m91@1.2.0
# Use this checkout's built SDK in the temporary application.
rm -rf /tmp/ai-m91/node_modules/ai
ln -s "$PWD/packages/ai" /tmp/ai-m91/node_modules/ai
node /tmp/ai-m91/verify.mjs
```

```js
import { generateText, isStepCount, jsonSchema, tool } from 'ai';
import { MockLanguageModelV4 } from 'ai/test';
import { createM91ToolApproval } from '@msg91comm/m91/integrations/vercel-ai';
globalThis.fetch = async () => { throw new Error('Network disabled for local verification'); };
const usage = { inputTokens: { total: 1, noCache: 1, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }, outputTokens: { total: 1, text: 1, reasoning: 0 } };
for (const decision of ['approve', 'reject', 'error']) {
  let executions = 0;
  let questions = 0;
  let modelCalls = 0;
  const client = { requestApproval: async () => { questions++; if (decision === 'error') throw new Error('offline service failure'); return decision === 'approve'; } };
  const issueRefund = tool({ description: 'Simulate a refund; no payment system is contacted.', inputSchema: jsonSchema({ type: 'object', properties: { orderId: { type: 'string' }, amount: { type: 'number' } }, required: ['orderId', 'amount'] }), execute: async input => { executions++; return { simulated: true, ...input }; } });
  const model = new MockLanguageModelV4({ doGenerate: async () => ++modelCalls === 1
    ? { content: [{ type: 'tool-call', toolCallId: 'call', toolName: 'issueRefund', input: JSON.stringify({ orderId: 'TEST', amount: 48 }) }], finishReason: { unified: 'tool-calls', raw: 'tool_calls' }, usage, warnings: [] }
    : { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'done' }], finishReason: { unified: 'stop', raw: 'stop' }, usage, warnings: [] } });
  const result = await generateText({ model, tools: { issueRefund }, toolApproval: createM91ToolApproval(client, { tools: ['issueRefund'], timeoutSeconds: 600 }), stopWhen: isStepCount(5), prompt: 'Simulate the refund.' });
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ decision, questions, executions, text: result.text }));
}
```

Observed output:

```json
{"decision":"approve","questions":1,"executions":1,"text":"done"}
{"decision":"reject","questions":1,"executions":0,"text":"done"}
{"decision":"error","questions":1,"executions":0,"text":"done"}
```

No verification-only files are committed.

## Background

community provider, which implements AI SDK 7's V4 interfaces for
language, embedding, speech and transcription models.

published provider declarations and local SDK. Provider factories,
option types and model IDs were checked against the published package
and model catalog. Both changed MDX files pass repository formatting.

`2157a43044c7f1c4cf1bfc73812cb23bc7e300a6` and found no blockers. All
four commits have verified signatures.

verification below.

## End-to-End Verification

Independent review did not run live inference: no ZeroGPU credentials
are configured. Published declarations and source corroborate the
documented API surface; the live-service results and performance claims
were not independently measured.

The following live results were supplied by the contributor in this PR.
They are retained as contributor evidence, not a new independent run.

Every code example on the page was run against the live ZeroGPU API with
the published `@zerogpu/ai-sdk-provider@0.1.1` (installed from npm, with
provenance attestation) and `ai@7.0.157`:

| Example | Result | Output |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
|
| Default `zerogpu` provider instance | Pass | `specificationVersion:
'v4'` |
| `createZeroGPU({ apiKey })` | Pass | `"Hey there, friend!"` |
| `zerogpu('gpt-oss-120b')` | Pass | `zerogpu.chat gpt-oss-120b v4` |
| `generateText` with `gpt-oss-120b` | Pass | `"## Vegetarian Lasagna
(Serves 4) ..."` |
| `streamText` with `gpt-oss-120b` | Pass | 9 text deltas, `"1 2 3 4 5"`
|
| Classification with `zlm-v1-iab-classify-edge` | Pass |
`{"audience":[{"name":"Laptops","score":0.79}, ...]}` |
| GLiNER `metadata` with `gliner2.5-base-v1` | Pass |
`{"entities":{"programming language":["Python
3.11"],"database":["PostgreSQL 15"]}}` |
| `deberta-v3-small` with labels in `instructions` | Pass |
`{"Sports":0.996,"Technology":0.003,"Finance":0.001}` |
| `embed` with `bge-small-en-v1.5` / `all-minilm-l6-v2` | Pass | 384 /
384 dimensions |
| `generateSpeech` with `chatterbox-nano` | Pass | `audio/mpeg`, 28,845
bytes written to `speech.mp3` |
| `transcribe` with `whisper-tiny` | Pass | `"Hello from zero GPU."`
(transcribing the generated `speech.mp3`) |

The tables and options on the page were also checked live:

- **Language model capabilities:** each of the 14 language models was
called, and every capability marked as supported works: text generation,
`Output.object`, tool calls, streamed tool calls, and image input on the
six image models.
- **Classification and extraction models:** all eight return parseable
JSON.
- **Speech and transcription:** `chatterbox-nano` returns audio in all
six output formats, and warns that `instructions`, `speed` and
`language` are unsupported. `whisper-tiny` returns the text, the
language (`en`), the duration (1.72s) and segments.
- **Provider options:** `reasoningEffort`, `metadata`, `categories`,
`maxKeywords`, the speech options (`seed`, `temperature`, `topP`,
`topK`, `repetitionPenalty`) and the transcription options (`language`,
`temperature`) are all accepted.
- **Model IDs and links:** every model ID on the page is in the [ZeroGPU
model catalog](https://docs.zerogpu.ai/docs/model-catalog), and every
link resolves.

fix(ai): download deprecated tool-result URLs and normalize media types (#21801)

## Background

Deprecated `file-url` and `image-url` tool-result content bypassed the
download plan. Models that require inline file bytes received remote
URLs instead. Downloaded generic media types also need normalization
before reaching providers.

## Summary

Include legacy URL content in downloads for ordinary tool messages and
provider-executed assistant results. Reuse file conversion to resolve
downloaded bytes and concrete media types, preserving provider options
and original URLs when passed through. Add regression coverage and a
patch changeset. Remove the committed reproduction; the complete
runnable script is below.

Validation: 77 prompt-conversion tests pass in Node and Edge, including
supported-URL passthrough, original URL/provider options, and media-type
normalization. Full workspace type checking and lint pass. Claude Code
Opus found no blockers; its suggested base64 data-URL regression and
release-note clarification are incorporated.

## Contributor Credit

@feiiiiii5 authored the fix and initial regression tests. @gr2m rebased
and signed the contributor commits, expanded role/passthrough coverage
and performed before/after verification.

## End-to-End Verification

Ran the same temporary application using the public `generateText` API
and the checkout's built `ai` package before (`045406280ae0`, whose core
implementation matches main) and after this fix. It exercises ordinary
tool results and provider-executed assistant results with PDF and PNG
assets.

Before: both runs log an empty downloads list and the model receives
`data.type: "url"` with generic `application`/`image` types. After: both
URLs reach the downloader with `isUrlSupportedByModel: false`, the model
receives inline byte arrays with concrete `application/pdf` and
`image/png` types, and the custom provider options remain intact. Both
calls return `done`.

Prerequisites: installed repository dependencies, supported Node and
pnpm. Save the complete script below outside the checkout as
`/tmp/ai-legacy-tool-urls.mjs`. From **each checkout**, run:

```bash
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai...
(cd examples/ai-functions && node --input-type=module < /tmp/ai-legacy-tool-urls.mjs)
```

The stdin execution resolves the local workspace package links in
`examples/ai-functions/node_modules`; no published SDK packages or
committed reproduction files are used.

**Verification limit:** this public SDK replay uses
`MockLanguageModelV4` to log the final model prompt and
`experimental_download` to supply deterministic bytes. It verifies the
application's SDK conversion/download flow, not a live provider or
network download. No provider credentials are configured, so
live-provider verification could not run. The original deprecation
warnings remain expected.

```js
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { MockLanguageModelV4 } from 'ai/test';

const pdf = new TextEncoder().encode('%PDF-1.7 example document');
const png = new Uint8Array([137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10]);
for (const role of ['tool', 'assistant']) {
  const requests = [];

fix(ai): download deprecated tool-result URLs and normalize media types (#21801)

## Background

Deprecated `file-url` and `image-url` tool-result content bypassed the
download plan. Models that require inline file bytes received remote
URLs instead. Downloaded generic media types also need normalization
before reaching providers.

## Summary

Include legacy URL content in downloads for ordinary tool messages and
provider-executed assistant results. Reuse file conversion to resolve
downloaded bytes and concrete media types, preserving provider options
and original URLs when passed through. Add regression coverage and a
patch changeset. Remove the committed reproduction; the complete
runnable script is below.

Validation: 77 prompt-conversion tests pass in Node and Edge, including
supported-URL passthrough, original URL/provider options, and media-type
normalization. Full workspace type checking and lint pass. Claude Code
Opus found no blockers; its suggested base64 data-URL regression and
release-note clarification are incorporated.

## Contributor Credit

@feiiiiii5 authored the fix and initial regression tests. @gr2m rebased
and signed the contributor commits, expanded role/passthrough coverage
and performed before/after verification.

## End-to-End Verification

Ran the same temporary application using the public `generateText` API
and the checkout's built `ai` package before (`045406280ae0`, whose core
implementation matches main) and after this fix. It exercises ordinary
tool results and provider-executed assistant results with PDF and PNG
assets.

Before: both runs log an empty downloads list and the model receives
`data.type: "url"` with generic `application`/`image` types. After: both
URLs reach the downloader with `isUrlSupportedByModel: false`, the model
receives inline byte arrays with concrete `application/pdf` and
`image/png` types, and the custom provider options remain intact. Both
calls return `done`.

Prerequisites: installed repository dependencies, supported Node and
pnpm. Save the complete script below outside the checkout as
`/tmp/ai-legacy-tool-urls.mjs`. From **each checkout**, run:

```bash
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai...
(cd examples/ai-functions && node --input-type=module < /tmp/ai-legacy-tool-urls.mjs)
```

The stdin execution resolves the local workspace package links in
`examples/ai-functions/node_modules`; no published SDK packages or
committed reproduction files are used.

**Verification limit:** this public SDK replay uses
`MockLanguageModelV4` to log the final model prompt and
`experimental_download` to supply deterministic bytes. It verifies the
application's SDK conversion/download flow, not a live provider or
network download. No provider credentials are configured, so
live-provider verification could not run. The original deprecation
